blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — skin assessment and accurate pressure-injury staging
stem: A sacral pressure injury has partial-thickness skin loss with exposed, moist red-pink dermis. No adipose tissue, granulation tissue, slough, or eschar is visible. How should the nurse stage this injury?

options.A: Stage 1 pressure injury; intact-skin staging is appropriate when adipose and deeper structures are not visible.
options.B: Deep tissue pressure injury; the moist red-pink surface may represent deeper damage evolving beneath disrupted skin.
options.C: Unstageable pressure injury; the wound base must be debrided before depth can be assigned when dermis is exposed.
options.D: Stage 2 pressure injury; partial-thickness loss exposes viable dermis without visible adipose, slough, or eschar.

rationale: D is correct. The current National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel staging definition identifies Stage 2 pressure injury as partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis. The wound bed is viable, pink or red, and moist; adipose and deeper tissues are not visible, and granulation tissue, slough, and eschar are absent. A is incorrect because Stage 1 requires intact skin with non-blanchable erythema. B is incorrect because deep tissue pressure injury is characterized by persistent non-blanchable deep red, maroon, or purple discoloration or related deep-tissue findings rather than a viable exposed-dermis wound bed meeting Stage 2 criteria. C is incorrect because unstageable pressure injury requires obscuring slough or eschar that prevents confirmation of the depth of full-thickness tissue loss; the stem explicitly states that neither is present.
educational_objective: Identify a Stage 2 pressure injury from partial-thickness skin loss with exposed viable dermis and absence of visible adipose, granulation tissue, slough, or eschar.
source_organization: National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel (NPIAP); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: NPIAP Pressure Injury Stages; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: NPIAP staging definitions derived from the 2016 consensus system and remain the current NPIAP staging framework when rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: NPIAP Pressure Injury Stages, Stage 2 Pressure Injury definition: partial-thickness loss of skin with exposed dermis; wound bed viable, pink/red and moist; adipose and deeper tissues are not visible; granulation tissue, slough and eschar are not present. The same document distinguishes Stage 1 as intact skin with non-blanchable erythema and Unstageable Pressure Injury as obscured full-thickness skin/tissue loss due to slough or eschar. Current NPIAP educational pages continue to use the NPIAP 2016 staging consensus framework. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Basic Care and Comfort, printed page 11 / PDF screenshot pageno 14: perform skin assessment and implement measures to maintain skin/tissue integrity.

option_audit.C: Plausible depth-uncertainty distractor; incorrect because unstageable injury requires obscuring slough or eschar and neither is present.
